summary: Andrew Glass specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed an MA (2000) and PhD (2006) at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon, and also studied at Bukkyo University (2003).

Andrew Goudie is an archaeologist and historian who studied at Dean Close School (~1958–1963) and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1964–1970). He served as a professor at the University of Oxford from 1970 to 2014.
Andrew J. Nicholson works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Shrinarayan Mishra and holds a post at Stony Brook University.

Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as executive director at the Insight Meditation Society, at the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and at the Mind & Life Institute (attested 2014).

Andrew P. Tuck works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Princeton University, with teachers including Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, Robert A. F. Thurman, Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and Richard Rorty.

Andrew Quintman is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Jay L. Garfield. Attested in 2015, he served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.
Andrew Sihler is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard (~1958–1962) and at Yale (~1962–1967) under Warren Cowgill. He held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from ~1967 to 1998.

Andrew Watsky specializes in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College (~1975–1979) and Princeton University (~1986–1994), and held a post at Vassar College from ~1994 to 2008.
Andrew William Kennedy is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 2006) under the doctoral supervision of Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Andrey Klebanov specializes in Indology and linguistics. He earned an MA (2010) and PhD (2016) at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson, later holding posts at Hamburg (attested 2015) and as professor at Kyoto University (attested 2018–2021).

Andrey Terentyev is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied in the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University (~1970–1975). He held a post at the Museum of the History of Religion (~1984–1998).

Andrzej Gawroński (1885–1927) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (1902–1906) and Leipzig (~1904–1907). He held posts at Jagiellonian University (1916–1917) and the University of Lviv as full professor and department head (1917).

András Róna-Tas is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, later serving as professor at the University of Szeged (1968–2002) and president of the IATS (~1979–1985).

André Bareau (1921–1993) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the Sorbonne and EPHE under Jean Filliozat, and held posts at the CNRS (1947–1951), EPHE (1956–1973), and Collège de France (1971–1991).

André Caquot (1923–2004) was a religious studies scholar and linguist educated at the École Normale Supérieure and EPHE. He held posts at EPHE (~1955–1972), University of Strasbourg (1957–1960), University of Paris (1964–1968), and Collège de France (1972–1994).

André Couture is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Laval University (~1965–1971), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1971–1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1971–1977), and held a post at Laval University (~1979).

André Godard (1881–1965) worked in archaeology, history, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts (~1900–1908) and held a post at the University of Tehran (~1934–1953).

André Martinet (1908–1999) was a linguist who studied at the Sorbonne and Berlin under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the EPHE (~1938–1946), Columbia University (~1947–1955), and the University of Paris (~1955–1977).
André Mazon (1881–1967) was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and the University of Prague (~1903–1904). He held a post at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.

André Padoux (1920–2017) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris under Louis Renou and Olivier Lacombe. He directed the Institut Français Frankfurt (~1959–1964) and held posts at the CNRS (1959, 1982).
